findings.description: The `APPEND_ONLY_DIR` WHY comment still says docs/adr/ holds "the index each new one adds a line to (decision 109)". Since 0133 there is no committed index, so drop that clause. The append-only claim about landed decisions still holds.

`--check` never compares the number in a decision's title with the 4-digit prefix of its filename. The duplicate error says "renumber the newer file", but a rename that leaves `# 0135. Foo` in `0136-foo.md` still passes and prints `[0135. Foo](0136-foo.md)`.

The rewritten `gateAndMerge` catch comment ("a resolved stop would go on through rebase state…") now explains why code that was deleted is absent. Under AGENTS.md §Comments it could simply be removed.
After the deletion, `mergeTargetInto`'s JSDoc ends in a short orphaned line ("…(decision 50). Returns the failure" / "for the worker, …"). Re-wrap it to the file's width.

README tension: the "Reading and writing" bullet still lets a later change "append an amendment section" to a landed decision, which is a second edit path into a landed file and runs against 0133's header-conflict rationale. The "(older files also carry `- Amended by:`)" aside in the format line repeats the bullet at lines 22-23.
The decision-file glob `"$ADR_DIR"/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md` appears twice, once in `index()` and once in the duplicate check, so a change to the naming convention needs both edits.
No package script, hook or workflow runs `scripts/adr-index.test.sh`, so the new duplicate-number and print-mode tests only run by hand. The base branch was the same.
